scope: Five primary studies. Human evidence and engineering hypotheses are kept separate. No clinical advice, universal smoothness claim, or novelty claim.

sources.authors: Papaxanthis C, Pozzo T, McIntyre J
sources.title: Arm end-point trajectories under normal and micro-gravity environments
sources.access: Complete primary abstract from PubMed and publisher; full methods not inspected.
sources.evidence: Two cosmonauts; changes in curvature and speed timing during space flight.
sources.limit: Very small sample; no universal smoothness or jerk result.

sources.authors: Macaluso T, Bourdin C, Buloup F, Mille ML, Sainton P, Sarlegna FR, Vercher JL, Bringoux L
sources.title: Sensorimotor Reorganizations of Arm Kinematics and Postural Strategy for Functional Whole-Body Reaching Movements in Microgravity
sources.access: Full publisher methods, results and discussion.
sources.evidence: Seven participants; brief parabolic flight; retained function with changed braking and posture.
sources.limit: Foot restraint, prior exposure, short duration, and different sampling/filtering; not a jerk comparison.

sources.title: The coordination of arm movements: an experimentally confirmed mathematical model
sources.access: Complete primary abstract and indexed first page of author PDF; full PDF open failed in this pass.
sources.evidence: Minimum integrated squared hand jerk predicted planar reaching features.
sources.limit: Kinematic model agreement does not identify a neural implementation.

sources.authors: Burdet E, Osu R, Franklin DW, Milner TE, Kawato M
sources.title: The central nervous system stabilizes unstable dynamics by learning optimal impedance
sources.access: Full primary article PDF; methods and results inspected. Despite the PDF filename, the article is in Nature.
sources.evidence: Learned directional stiffness in a robotic divergent force field.
sources.limit: Endpoint stiffness estimates at 120-180 ms do not isolate passive muscle mechanics.

sources.authors: Crevecoeur F, Thonnard JL, Lefevre P, Scott SH
sources.title: Long-Latency Feedback Coordinates Upper-Limb and Hand Muscles during Object Manipulation Tasks
sources.access: Primary methods and discussion excerpts refreshed; full article inspected for earlier neuroscience report. Direct publisher/PMC open failed during this pass.
sources.evidence: Sixteen participants; coordinated goal-dependent responses near 60 ms.
sources.limit: Does not identify one circuit, fixed planning cadence, or universal damper.

unsupported_claims: Human movement is identical on Earth and in microgravity.
The brain literally runs a minimum-jerk solver on every update.
One passive damper explains human smoothness.
A gravity-independent neural continuity layer has been identified.
All synthetic motion lacks trajectory smoothing.
engineering_inference: Keep state across goal changes; prove the chosen continuity order, tracking error, lag, effort and stopping reserve separately from the biological analogy.
